config.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala

personas.name: Yvonne
personas.goals: Fund four more beds this year
personas.hidden_agenda: The shelter turned away eleven women last month

personas.name: Graham
personas.goals: A gala that costs a lot less than it raises

personas.name: Pilar
personas.goals: An evening that moves people to give
personas.hidden_agenda: Booked the keynote speaker before checking the fee with the board

personas.name: Jerome
personas.hidden_agenda: Two companies said maybe and he counted them

agenda.title: Budget and goal
agenda.goal: Check the budget against the fundraising goal

agenda.title: Speakers and program
agenda.goal: Settle the keynote and the survivor speaker

facts.statement: Each $10,000 funds one shelter bed for a year

beats.summary: Budget, goal and last year; Yvonne's memory of last year is high, corrected later
The keynote and the survivor speaker; Pilar's fee figure stands
Corporate tables; Jerome's count is high; an off-topic stretch about a new restaurant

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Thank you for coming. This gala matters more than usual this year. We turned women away last month.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: The budget for the evening is thirty-eight thousand. The goal is two hundred thousand.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Last year we raised a hundred and eighty, so two hundred is a stretch but not a fantasy.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: And this year we have the matching pledge. Twenty-five thousand, if we raise it first.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: The matching pledge is a great story for the paddle raise. Every dollar doubled.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: What does a bed cost us, for the paddle raise? People like to know what their money does.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: Ten thousand funds one bed for a year.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: So the paddle raise could literally be "fund a bed". That's powerful.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: That's exactly what I want. Four beds is the dream.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: Sorry, a small thing. Last year's total, was it a hundred and eighty? My notes have a hundred and sixty-four.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Oh. You're probably right. A hundred and eighty was the pledges, before a few fell through.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: A hundred and sixty-four, then. So two hundred is a bigger jump than it sounded.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: The program. I've booked Dana Whitlock as the keynote. She's wonderful, and the fee is five thousand.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: That's a lot for a speech, in my opinion.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: She brings people. Last time she spoke at a gala, they raised a fortune.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: The survivor speaker matters more to me than the keynote. Who is it this year?

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: Rosa, from our transitional housing. She asked to do it. She's been practicing.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Rosa. That's brave of her. We need to make sure she's supported that night.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: Could she speak before dinner instead of after? People are more focused before the wine.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: She wanted to speak right before the paddle raise. That's when it matters most.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Then Rosa speaks right before the paddle raise, and the keynote opens the evening.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: I'll tell Rosa tomorrow and schedule a rehearsal with her at the hotel.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: Has Dana's contract been signed by the board?

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: Not yet. I signed the letter of intent myself.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: That's not how it works, Pilar.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: I know. It was going to go to someone else. I'm sorry.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Let's get the contract to the board this week and do it properly.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: Tables. We've sold twelve corporate tables, at three thousand each.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: Twelve? I only have nine invoices, I think. Maybe I'm missing some?

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: No, you're right. Nine paid. Three said yes on the phone but haven't signed.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Then nine, until they sign.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: I'll chase the three this week. One of them is the bank, and they always come through.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: Individual tickets are at two hundred and ten. The ballroom holds three twenty.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: So plenty of room for the last tables.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: Has anyone been to that new Lebanese place on Fifth? I took the bank people there and they loved it.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: The one with the garden? I want to go. I hear the bread is incredible.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: My wife's been twice already. She says the lamb is the best in the city.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: We should eat there to celebrate when this is over. Back to tables, though.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: Could the board members each bring a table of friends? That's how other galas fill up.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: Some can. Some of us are the friends.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Let's ask every board member to host a table or buy two tickets. Not a requirement. An ask.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: Logistics. We have thirty-five volunteers so far.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Is that enough? Last year felt thin at check-in.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: For check-in, yes. For the auction tables, we need about five more.

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: The high school's service club helped another charity last month. They were very good.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: Someone ought to read the hotel's cancellation terms too, just in case.

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: I'll call their advisor on Monday.

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.text: The date's November fifteenth for everything, including the hotel contract?

turns.speaker: Pilar
turns.text: The fifteenth. The hotel, the caterer and Dana are all booked for that night.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Who's taking care of Rosa on the night, so she isn't alone before she speaks?

turns.speaker: Graham
turns.text: I'll have a budget update for the next meeting, with the keynote fee in it.

turns.speaker: Yvonne
turns.text: Thank you. We'll fund those beds.
